calls.head: Carlsson gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Islanders keep sending Pageau’s line (Heineman, Pageau and Duclair) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Peter DeBoer has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Ducks’ first line is Killorn, Carlsson and Klepov.

calls.body: On the penalty kill, Anaheim is near the top of the league, but the Islanders are one of the worst. Penalties should hurt the Islanders more than the Ducks. Anaheim’s penalty kill has been near the bottom of the league for years, though.

surprises.head: The Islanders picked Anaheim’s defense apart
surprises.body: Anaheim usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: the Islanders’ shots at 5-on-5 had an 8.7% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% (about 6.5% against Anaheim) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

story.head: The Islanders beat the Ducks
paras: It was a busy first period. Ondřej Palát and Victor Eklund scored less than three minutes apart late in the period to put the Islanders up 2-0. Frank Vatrano got the Ducks on the board 50 seconds later. Simon Holmström stretched the lead to 3-1 on the power play a minute and a half later, and that goal turned out to be the winner. A.J. Greer and Mitchell Chaffee dropped the gloves midway through the second. The Ducks’ Pavel Mintyukov left late in the period and didn’t return. With the goalie pulled and less than three minutes left, Alex Killorn pulled the Ducks within one, but the Islanders held on.

The Islanders dominated, and the replays agree: run this game’s chances back a hundred times and the Islanders win about four in five. Ilya Sorokin made 15 saves for the Isles, and Lukáš Dostál stopped 22 of 25. The Islanders improved to 5-3-1, and the Ducks dropped to 4-5-0.
